Comprehensive adjustment of Toe, Camber, and Caster angles to factory specifications.
Full suspension and steering linkage inspection.

Checking for uneven tyre wear and pressure.

1. Wheel Alignment Section
This refers to the adjustment of the vehicle's suspension settings.
Computerized Wheel Alignment (4-Wheel): The service of checking and adjusting the angles of all four wheels.
Caster, Camber, and Toe Adjustment: These are the technical names for the angles being corrected.
Steering Centering: Ensuring the steering wheel is perfectly straight when the car is moving forward.
2. Wheel Balancing Section
This refers to ensuring the weight of the tyre and rim is distributed evenly.
Wheel Balancing Labor: The service charge for spinning the wheels on a balancing machine.
Wheel Weights (Lead/Zinc/Steel): You will see a separate line item for the physical weights added to your rims. It is often billed "per gram" or "per unit."
Example: "Wheel Weights - 40g" or "Sticker Weights - 4 units."
3. Additional Common Descriptions
Tyre Rotation: Changing the position of the tyres (e.g., moving rear tyres to the front) to ensure even wear.
Nitrogen Inflation / Top-up: Charging for filling tyres with Nitrogen instead of regular air.
Valves/Nozzles: If your tyre valves were leaking and replaced, they will be listed as "Tubeless Valves.".
